newsitem.title: USA: Standard Management int'l sales decline.
newsitem.headline: Standard Management int'l sales decline.

text.p: Standard Management Corp said it recorded higher domestic sales of flexible premium deferred annuities in 1996 as well as higher unaffiliated annuity products, though its international sales fell 45.8 percent.

Raymond Ohlson, president of Standard Life Insurance Co of Indiana and a director of Standard Management International S.A. (SMISA), said the decline in international sales was due to a restructuring of those operations.
Ohlson said the company's international operations "already produced positive results for the first four months of SMISA's 1997 fiscal year (SMISA reports on a fiscal yearend of September 30)."

Domestically, Standard Life Insurance said its 1996 annuity sales rose 31 percent to $48.9 million over 1995's totals. Unaffiliated annuity product sales increased 28 percent in 1996 to $21.3 million, it added.
"Although we saw a decline in sales in our international operations during 1996, we actually saw an increase in operational earnings in SMISA," Ohlson noted.
